# Contributing to Kalapriti Designs

This repository contains the website for **Kalapriti Designs**, an architectural and design
consultancy. It is a client project: the code is owned by Kalapriti Designs and is designed, built
and maintained by the [Stackified](https://github.com/stackified) team. The repository is public for
portfolio purposes, so day-to-day development is done by Stackified rather than through outside
contributions.

Bug reports are welcome through [issues](https://github.com/stackified/kalapriti/issues). For
security problems, follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) instead of opening a public issue.

## Getting set up

The site is a React 19 single-page app built with Vite. You need Node.js 22 (the version CI uses)
and npm.

1. Clone the repository and switch to the `dev` branch:
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/stackified/kalapriti.git
   cd kalapriti
   git checkout dev
   ```
2. Install dependencies:
   ```bash
   npm ci
   ```
3. Start the development server:
   ```bash
   npm run dev
   ```
   Then open `http://localhost:5173/`.

Other useful commands:

```bash
npm run lint      # ESLint
npm run build     # production build to dist/
npm run preview   # serve the built dist/ locally
npm run images    # regenerate AVIF/WebP variants (Python + Pillow)
```

`npm run deploy` also exists (it builds and publishes `dist/` to the `gh-pages` branch), but
production deploys normally go through CI, which runs the build checks first. See the branch flow
below.

## Project structure

- `src/data/` - all copy and settings: `site.js` (brand, contact details, navigation, feature
  flags, `asset()`), `services.js`, `process.js`, `projects.js`, `resources.js`, and the generated
  image manifest `images.js`
- `src/pages/` - Home, Projects, Services, Process, Resources, About, Contact, NotFound
- `src/components/` - Layout, Nav, Footer, PageHeader, Reveal, Picture, FloatingActions, Cursor,
  Atmosphere
- `src/lib/motion.js` - the single GSAP and ScrollTrigger entry point
- `src/index.css` - design tokens; `src/App.css` - component styles
- `public/` - `assets/` (logo, images), `CNAME`, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`
- `scripts/images.py` - responsive image pipeline
- `vite.config.js` - base path and the generated `404.html` SPA fallback
- `docs/` - brand values, corporate structure and SEO keyword notes

## Rules that keep the site working

These follow the rules documented in the README. Breaking them has broken production before.

- **Deploy base path**: `vite.config.js` is the only place the base path is set. It reads
  `VITE_BASE` and defaults to `/` for the custom domain. Never write the base path anywhere else.
- **Asset URLs**: build every URL to a file in `public/` with `asset()` from `src/data/site.js`,
  which reads `import.meta.env.BASE_URL`. Never hardcode a path prefix in a component.
- **Brand strings**: take them from `BRAND` in `src/data/site.js`. Do not type the brand name inline.
- **Content**: services, process steps, contact details and navigation live in `src/data/`. Change
  the data file, not the component.
- **Motion**: import GSAP from `src/lib/motion.js`, never from `gsap` directly, and keep every
  animation readable under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **SPA fallback**: `dist/404.html` is generated by `vite.config.js` at build time. Do not add a
  static `public/404.html`, and keep the restore snippet in `index.html` in step with it.
- **Images**: add originals to `public/assets`, add a `PLAN` entry in `scripts/images.py`, run
  `npm run images`, then use `<Picture name="..." />`. Do not edit `src/data/images.js` by hand.
- **ESLint**: a capitalised parameter used only as a JSX tag is reported as unused. Bind it to a
  `const` instead (see `Reveal.jsx`).

## Branch flow

- `main` is the default branch and the production branch.
- `dev` is the integration branch.
- Work happens on short-lived branches cut from `dev`, named like `feat/short-description`,
  `fix/short-description` or `chore/short-description`.

The `build-and-deploy` workflow runs on pushes and pull requests to `dev` and `main`. Every run
installs with `npm ci`, then runs lint, build, and a verify step that checks the build output
(root-relative asset URLs, no leftover `/kalapriti/` subpath, `CNAME`, and the `404.html` fallback).

1. Open a pull request from your branch into `dev`. CI must pass. Pushes to `dev` run the same
   checks but never deploy.
2. When `dev` is ready, open a pull request from `dev` into `main`.
3. A push to `main` runs the checks and then publishes `dist/` to the `gh-pages` branch, which
   GitHub Pages serves at https://kalapritidesigns.com.

## Making changes

1. Create a branch from `dev`: `git checkout -b fix/short-description`
2. Keep changes focused. One feature or fix per pull request.
3. Match the existing style: plain CSS with the tokens in `index.css`, function components, and
   content in `src/data/`.
4. Run `npm run lint` and `npm run build`, then check the affected pages in the browser at desktop
   and mobile widths, including a deep link such as `/services`.

## Pull requests

1. Push your branch and open a pull request against `dev`.
2. Fill in the pull request template: what changed, why, and how you tested it.
3. Link any related issue (for example, `Closes #12`).
4. Releases to production are a separate pull request from `dev` into `main`.

For security issues, follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) instead of opening a public issue.
